title: Show active encode or remux route in top bar
summary: Add a compact active-route badge to the top-bar activity card using the established green remux and blue encode semantic colors.
reason: The compact activity card identifies the current title and run state but does not make the backend-confirmed remux-versus-encode route visible at a glance.
behavior_before: The top-bar activity card showed the current title and run metadata without an encode or remux label.
behavior_after: Fresh backend-confirmed current work shows a REMUX or ENCODE badge beside the title. Mixed concurrent routes show both badges, while stale, unavailable, or route-undecided evidence shows no badge.
tests_added: Added static coverage for the backend-route badge projection and semantic remux/encode styling.
Extended the browser Run Monitor smoke to verify remux, hardware encode, and CPU fallback routes render the expected badge category.
manual_validation: All eight Rung 1 non-browser WebView smoke wrappers passed.

Bundled-Python tests.webview.test_webview_browser_run_monitor_smoke - 1 passed in Chrome, including undecided-route suppression, distinct remux/encode computed colors, encode aliases, and mixed concurrent routes.

Test-WebViewBrowserHomeLiveStateSmoke did not reach badge rendering because the current broader worktree is missing the pre-existing renderCloseReadiness global expected by that smoke; no packet-owned file defines or exports that function.

The repository-wide release self-test exceeded the 120-second capture window, continued through desktop/tooling/generated checks, and later exited without a recoverable exit code; it is not counted as a pass.
node syntax, 14 static Run Monitor tests, targeted Chrome Run Monitor smoke, and all eight non-browser WebView smokes passed; strict worktree coverage passed
rollback_plan: Remove the top-bar route categorization and badge renderer, remove the activity-route badge CSS, and revert the matching static and browser assertions.
notes: Read-only WebView projection only. No FFmpeg, route-decision, media-policy, queue, process-lifecycle, source, scratch, publish, subtitle, audio, or backend behavior changes. No Python production files changed. Representative real-media validation is not required for this display-only change.
